t.1.89.1: Janamejaya said: Blessed one, I wish to hear of the kings who founded and continued the lineage of Pūru, of what valour they were, of what kind, how many they were, and of what prowess.
t.1.89.2: For never before in this lineage has there been a king of men who was lacking in virtuous conduct, or devoid of valor, or bereft of offspring.
t.1.89.3: O ascetic rich in austerity, I wish to hear in detail the deeds of those kings of renowned conduct, who were endowed with wisdom.
t.1.89.4: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Very well, I shall tell you what you ask of me: of the heroes who upheld the lineage of Pūru, whose splendor was equal to Śakra's.
t.1.89.5: Pravīra, Īśvara and Raudrāśva, three sons who were great chariot-warriors, were born to Pūru by Pauṣṭī; among them Pravīra was the founder of the lineage.
t.1.89.6: From him was born Manasyu, the heroic and mighty lord, son of Śyenī, lotus-eyed protector of the earth bounded by the four seas.
t.1.89.7: Subhrū, Saṃhanana and Vāgmin, the three sons of Sauvīrī, were born as the sons of Manasyu; all were heroes and great chariot-warriors.
t.1.89.8: Ten sons were born to Raudrāśva by an Apsaras, great archers, heroes, performers of sacrifice, blessed with offspring and deeply learned. All of them were versed in every weapon, and all were devoted to dharma.
t.1.89.9: Then there were Ṛcepu, Kakṣepu, and the valiant Kṛkaṇepu, Sthaṇḍilepu, Vanepu, and Sthalepu, the great chariot-warrior.
t.1.89.12: Of them, the mighty Taṃsu, carrying forward the lineage of Puru, won blazing glory and conquered the earth.
t.1.89.11: Then from Ṛcepu was born the learned King Matināra. The sons of Matināra, O king, were four, of boundless valor: Taṃsu, Mahān, Atiratha, and Druhyu of matchless splendor.
t.1.89.13: The valiant Taṃsu begot a son, Ilina; he too, the best of conquerors, conquered this entire earth.
t.1.89.10: Tejepu the strong and wise, Satyepu with the valor of Indra, Dharmepu, and Saṃnatepu, the tenth, with the valor of a god: these, dear son, were the sons of Anādhṛṣṭi, performers of the Rājasūya and the Aśvamedha sacrifices.
t.1.89.16: From Duḥṣanta was born Bharata, the wise king, son of Śakuntalā; from him the great fame of the lineage of Bharata spread far and wide.
t.1.89.15: He begot Duḥṣanta, Śūra and Bhīma, Prapūrva and Vasu as well. Of these, O Janamejaya, the eldest was Duḥṣanta, who became king.
t.1.89.14: Then, O king, he begot on Rathaṃtarī the five sons of Ilina, Duḥṣanta and the others, who were like the five elements.
t.1.89.18: Then Bharata, having sacrificed with great sacrifices, obtained at that time from Bharadvāja a son named Bhumanyu, O Bhārata.
t.1.89.19: Then, knowing himself to have a son, the delight of the Pauravas consecrated Bhumanyu as heir apparent, O best of the Bharatas.
t.1.89.17: Bharata begot nine sons on three wives, but the king did not rejoice in them, saying, “They are not worthy of me.”
t.1.89.22: The eldest of them, Suhotra, obtained the kingship of the earth-rulers. He offered many sacrifices, beginning with the Rājasūya and the Aśvamedha.
t.1.89.20: Then a little son was born to that great king, but in vain; thereupon that one, named Vitatha, became the son of Bhumanyu.
t.1.89.21: Suhotra, Suhotṛ, Suhavis, and likewise Suyajus were born to Puṣkariṇī as the sons of Ṛcīka Bhumanyu.
t.1.89.23: Suhotra enjoyed the whole earth, whose garment is the ocean, full of elephants, cattle and horses and teeming with many jewels.
t.1.89.24: His earth, oppressed by the immense burden, filled with elephants, horses and chariots and thickly crowded with men, seemed almost to sink.
t.1.89.26: O Bhārata, the Aikṣvākī princess bore to Suhotra, lord of the earth, Ajamīḍha, Sumīḍha, and Purumīḍha.
t.1.89.25: While King Suhotra then ruled his subjects according to dharma, the earth was marked with sanctuaries and sacrificial posts by the hundreds of thousands, and with its people and crops flourishing, it shone, together with the gods.
t.1.89.27: Ajamīḍha was the best of them, and in him the lineage was established. He too begot six sons on three wives, O Bhārata.
t.1.89.29: Likewise, O king, all these Pāñcālas are the descendants of Duḥṣanta and Parameṣṭhin, and the Kuśikas are the descendants of Jahnu of boundless splendor.
t.1.89.28: Dhūminī bore Ṛkṣa, and Nīlī bore Duḥṣanta and Parameṣṭhin; Keśinī bore Jahnu and the two, Jana and Rūpiṇa.
t.1.89.31: O king, while Saṃvaraṇa, the son of Ṛkṣa, was ruling the earth, there was a very great destruction of the people, so we have heard.
t.1.89.30: They say that Ṛkṣa, a lord of men, was the eldest of Jana and Rūpiṇa. From Ṛkṣa was born Saṃvaraṇa, O king, the founder of your lineage.
t.1.89.33: Shaking the earth with his fourfold army, the Pāñcāla, having swiftly conquered the earth, marched against him, and with ten akṣauhiṇīs he defeated him in battle.
t.1.89.32: Then the kingdom fell to ruin through many kinds of losses, stricken by hunger and death, by drought and by diseases; and the armies of their rivals struck down the Bhāratas.
t.1.89.34: Then King Saṃvaraṇa, together with his wives, his ministers, his sons and his friends, fled from that great danger.
t.1.89.36: While they were dwelling there for a thousand years, the blessed seer Vasiṣṭha then came to the Bharatas.
t.1.89.35: He then dwelt in a thicket by the great river Sindhu, at the edge of the river country, near a mountain. There the Bhāratas lived for a long time, having taken refuge in an inaccessible stronghold.
t.1.89.37: When he had arrived, all the Bhāratas went out eagerly to meet him and saluted him, offering him the guest-water, and with due honour they laid everything before the radiant seer.
t.1.89.38: When he had dwelt there into the eighth year, the king himself then chose him, saying, “Let your honor be our purohita; we are striving for the kingdom.” Saying “Om,” Vasiṣṭha too accepted the Bhāratas.
t.1.89.40: He occupied the finest of cities, formerly inhabited by the Bharatas, and once again he made all the kings of the earth bearers of tribute.
t.1.89.39: Then he consecrated the Paurava to imperial sovereignty over the whole kṣatriya order, as the horn, the foremost, upon all the earth; so we have heard.
t.1.89.41: Then the mighty Ājamīḍha, having regained the earth, sacrificed again with many great sacrifices rich in sacrificial fees.
t.1.89.42: Then Tapatī, daughter of the Sun, bore Kuru to Saṃvaraṇa. All the subjects chose him for kingship, saying, "He knows dharma."
t.1.89.43: By his name Kurujāṅgala became renowned upon the earth; that man of great austerity made Kurukṣetra holy through his austerity.
t.1.89.44: We have heard of his sons Aśvavant and Abhiṣvant, likewise Citraratha and Muni, and the renowned Janamejaya. These five sons the high-minded Vāhinī brought forth.
t.1.89.46: Uccaiḥśravas, Bhadrakāra, and Jitāri, who is remembered as the eighth; and in the lineage of these, they became renowned for the virtues born of their deeds.
t.1.89.45: From Abhiṣvant came Parikṣit, and the valiant Śabalāśva, Abhirāja, Virāja, and Śalmala of great strength.
t.1.89.47: Janamejaya and the others, seven in all, and likewise other men of great strength, were the sons of Parikṣit, all of them well versed in dharma and artha.
t.1.89.49: The sons of Janamejaya, renowned on earth and of great strength, were Dhṛtarāṣṭra the firstborn, Pāṇḍu, and Bāhlīka.
t.1.89.48: Kakṣasena and Ugrasena, the valiant Citrasena, Indrasena, Suṣeṇa, and one named Bhīmasena.
t.1.89.50: Niṣadha of great splendor, and likewise the mighty Jāmbūnada, Kuṇḍodara, Padāti, and Vasāti, who is known as the eighth; all were skilled in dharma and artha, and all delighted in the welfare of beings.
t.1.89.52: Three sons were born to Pratīpa, O bull of the Bharatas: Devāpi, Śaṃtanu, and Bāhlīka, the great chariot-warrior.
t.1.89.51: Then Dhṛtarāṣṭra became king, and his son was Kuṇḍika; there were also Hastin, Vitarka, Krātha, and Kuṇḍala as the fifth, as well as Haviḥśravas, Indrābha, and the unconquered Sumanyu.
t.1.89.54: In the lineage of Bharata, O king, were born many excellent kings, mighty in spirit, great chariot-warriors, equal to gods and seers.
t.1.89.53: Of them, Devāpi went forth into the ascetic life out of a desire to attain dharma, while Śaṃtanu obtained the earth, and so did Bāhlīka, the great chariot-warrior.
t.1.89.55: And other great chariot-warriors of this kind too, equal to the gods, were born in the line of Manu, increasing the lineage of Aila.
